# The critique loop

The main session keeps every critic finding in
`accord/tickets/<id>/plan-review.md`: one `## Round <n> (whole)` or
`## Round <n> (diff)` section per round, each finding on one line as
`<n>. <Must|Should|Nice> — <finding> — <state>`. The state is `open`,
`fixed`, `deferred` for a Nice, `unverified: <reason>`, `withdrawn`,
`repeated as <round>.<n>` when a critic carries it on under that number,
`open, owner: "<the owner's words>"` for a fix the owner said to apply,
or `owner: "<the owner's words>"` for one the owner dropped. After the
state the session copies the critic's marks, each as ` — <mark>`:
`rests on: <the ticket line>`, `risk: data-loss` or `risk: security`,
`test: <id>`, `command: <command>`. The separator is always ` — `, never a hyphen, and a risk is written exactly ` — risk: security` or ` — risk: data-loss` after the finding's text: accord reads a risk from that mark slot only, never from the finding's words, a note or a reason. A mark slot whose value does not parse (`risks: security`, `risk: data_loss`, `risk: security` in backticks or quotes) is a record problem, and `accord round <id> --plan` refuses it on a plan record written under accord 0.4.1 or later. A value that is no kind (`risk: none`) is prose. A finding stays `open` or `unverified` until a critic lists it after `fixed:` or
`withdrawn:`, or the owner drops it; the planner's word alone closes
nothing. A round with no findings says `No findings`. Only the sections
after the last `## Closed` line count; step 8 of the skill appends that
line.

`plan-review.md` starts with the line `Round record: 1`, above every heading; its only headings are `## Round <n> (whole)`, `## Round <n> (diff)` and `## Closed`. Before each round, and before step 8 of the skill appends `## Closed`, run `accord round <id> --plan`: exit 0 gives the round's number and the cap; it counts only the rounds after the last `## Closed` line: from accord 0.4.1 `accord round <id> --plan` counts at most three rounds, prints `stop: report to owner` from round 3 on a round that still reports a Should or a Must, and after any round whose Must + Should count did not fall from the round before, and on a third round that reports any finding; a ticket claimed under an older accord keeps five rounds and the stop from round 3 (`accord round <id> --plan` prints `of 5` for it), and a fifth round that reports any finding stops it. On a stop, stop and report to the owner what it prints, as `./ask.md` says, and ask whether to change course, accept the open findings, or allow more rounds. Write the answer as the last line `verdict: accepted-by-owner "<the owner's sentence>"` in `plan-review.md`, which ends the loop as step 4 says; or, to allow more rounds, as the ledger Ruling `Ruling: the owner allows <n> more plan critique rounds after round <r> of cycle <k> — "<the owner's sentence>" — <cost if wrong>`, with r and k as the stop printed them; or, for a change of course, as that same Ruling with n the rounds the owner gives the reworked plan, then the re-plan. A round after the stop, allowed by the owner, that reports no findings clears it. Never append `## Closed` while a stop holds. On a `refused:` that says the loop has ended, the loop is over: go to step 7 of the skill, or at step 8 append `## Closed`. On any other `refused:`, fix what it names and run it again.

1. **Read.** Round 1 is `whole`. Judge from the ticket and the plan
   whether the ticket touches auth, money, migration, or data deletion,
   or the plan touches a path under `sensitive:` in `accord/config.yml`.
   Dispatch in parallel, each in a fresh context, mode `plan`, with the
   paths of the ticket and `plan.md`:
   - one `accord-critic`, no lens, the plan checker, which runs every
     check of its fixed checklist, for a plan of any size;
   - one more `accord-critic`, lens `security`, when the ticket touches
     auth, money, migration, or data deletion, or the plan touches a path
     under `sensitive:` in `accord/config.yml`.

   The security critic runs in round 1 only; later rounds, whole or diff,
   verify its fixes, and a finding marked `risk: data-loss` or
   `risk: security` blocks in every round. The plan checker and every
   `diff` critic check the plan against every Decision and every
   Correction of the ticket.

   Merge and de-duplicate their findings into one round, numbered within
   it, before the planner gets them. After a round that reports a Must,
   or that leaves a Must from an earlier round open or unverified (its
   section holds a Must, or `<m>` is above zero in step 5), the next
   round is `whole`, even when the owner dropped that Must: one
   `accord-critic` in a fresh context, no lens, mode `plan`, with the
   paths of the ticket, `plan.md`, and `plan-review.md`. After any other
   round the next is `diff`: write
   `git diff <that round's commit> -- accord/tickets/<id>/plan.md`, which
   holds the planner's fix, into a file outside the working tree, and
   dispatch one `accord-critic` in a fresh context, mode `diff`, with the
   paths of the ticket, `plan.md`, that file, and `plan-review.md`. A
   `diff` critic never reads the whole plan.
2. **Record.** Append the round's section to `plan-review.md` and mark
   each new finding `open`. Mark `fixed` each finding a critic lists
   after `fixed:`, and `withdrawn` each one it lists after `withdrawn:`.
   When a new finding starts `repeats <round>.<n>:`, mark that earlier
   finding `repeated as <this round>.<n>`. A Nice goes to the ledger
   under `## Deferred`, marked `deferred`, and never to the planner.
   From round 2 (accord 0.4.1 and later), and from round 1 under the plan
   checker when `accord round <id> --plan` refuses round 2 naming such a
   finding, a new Must or Should with none of the marks above is marked
   `deferred` too and goes to the ledger
   under `## Deferred` as
   `- plan <r>.<n>[ cycle <k>]: <finding> — failing case: <case>`
   (` cycle <k>` from cycle 2 on), never to the planner. A finding with a
   `risk:` mark is never deferred: it blocks in every round.
3. **Owner.** A finding whose proposed fix relies on an API cited only
   by a URL outside the repository goes to the owner at once, as
   `./ask.md` says: show the finding, the fix, and the URL, and ask
   whether to apply or drop it. On apply its state becomes
   `open, owner: "<the owner's words>"`: it goes to the planner with
   those words, which confirm the API, and closes only when a critic
   lists it after `fixed:`. On drop its state becomes
   `owner: "<the owner's words>"`, which closes it.
4. **Converged.** The loop ends only on a round that reports no Must
   and no Should and leaves no Must or Should open or unverified, or on
   the owner's acceptance after a stop, the last line
   `verdict: accepted-by-owner "<the owner's sentence>"` of
   `plan-review.md`, and only when the last `accord gate plan <id>`
   passed (after an acceptance, run it once more): go to step 7 of the
   skill.
5. **Fix.** Otherwise commit `plan.md` and `plan-review.md` with the
   subject `plan: <id> round <n>, <m> Must, <s> Should`, where `<m>` and
   `<s>` count the Musts and the Shoulds after the last `## Closed` line
   that are `open` or `unverified` once this round is recorded; the next
   `diff` round reads from that commit. Dispatch `accord-planner` with the
   ticket path, the baseline, the mode, the path of `plan-review.md`, and
   every Must and Should that is `open` or `unverified`, never a Nice,
   each labelled `<round>.<n>` and listed with the owner's words it holds.
   The planner fixes every one and replies by that label. Write each
   `unverified: <reason>` it replies into the state of the finding with that
   label; a finding it reports fixed stays `open` until a critic lists it
   after `fixed:`. Tell the planner to change only the lines a finding
   needs, inside the tasks it names (`Task <n>` or `the preamble`).
   From accord 0.4.1, `accord round <id> --plan` lists the `plan.md`
   hunks outside the tasks the open findings of the cycle name and refuses
   them; on that refusal narrow the fix, or ask the owner, as `./ask.md`
   says, and write under `## Rulings` in the ledger
   `Ruling: the owner allows the plan fix after round <r> of cycle <k> to change <places> — "<the owner's sentence>" — <cost if wrong>`,
   where `<places>` is `Task <n>[, Task <m>…]`, `the preamble` or
   `the whole plan`; a re-plan after a change of course needs that Ruling
   with `the whole plan`. Then go back to step 4 of the skill.
